fields.claim_quote:
Let $m \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be such that:
:$3^m + 1 \le \size {2 n} \le 3^{m + 1} - 1$
where $\size {2 n}$ denotes the [[Definition:Absolute Value|absolute value]] of $2 n$.

As $2 n$ is [[Definition:Even Integer|even]], this is always possible, because $3^r$ is always an [[Definition:Odd Integer|odd integer]] for [[Definition:Non-Negative Integer|non-negative]] $r$.
fields.explanation: The proof starts with arbitraryintegern and asserts existence of nonnegativeexponentm. Zero is not excluded. Keepn=0. For everym,3^m+1>0=|2n|, so no admissiblemexists. Core Nat/Int exponent, absolutevalue and unbounded quantifier; no finite search is substituted for allm.
fields.flaw: For every integer n, there exists a nonnegative integer m such that 3^m + 1 ≤ |2n| ≤ 3^(m+1) − 1.
fields.problem:
Title: Representation of Integers in Balanced Ternary

Let $n \in \Z$ be an [[Definition:Integer|integer]].

$n$ can be represented [[Definition:Unique|uniquely]] in [[Definition:Balanced Ternary Representation|balanced ternary]]:

:$\ds n = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^m r_j 3^j$

:$\sqbrk {r_m r_{m - 1} \ldots r_2 r_1 r_0}$

such that:

where:
:$m \in \Z_{>0}$ is a [[Definition:Strictly Positive Integer|strictly positive integer]] such that $3^m < \size {2 n} < 3^{m + 1}$
:all the $r_j$ are such that $r_j \in \set {\underline 1, 0, 1}$, where $\underline 1 := -1$.

fields.witness: Take n = 0, an integer. Then |2n| = |0| = 0. For every nonnegative integer m, 3^m ≥ 1, so 3^m + 1 ≥ 2. Hence the required lower bound 3^m + 1 ≤ 0 is false. Therefore no admissible m exists.
